lessons.title: The Lesson: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
The Rashidun Caliphs

The first caliphate, the Rashidun Caliphate, was ruled by the four Rashidun (rightly-guided) caliphs: Hazrat Abu Bakr, Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali.

Caliphs were religious and political leaders of the Muslim world. They were close companions of Rasoolullah (peace be upon him). The Rashidun Caliphate lasted for 30 years and is a role model for all Muslim rulers.

There are four Rashidun Caliphs: Hazrat Abu Bakr, Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali.

The First Man to Accept Islam

Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique was the first among men to embrace Islam.

The Title 'Al-Farooq'

Al-Farooq means the one who distinguishes between the right and the wrong. Rasoolullah gave Hazrat Umar this title because he became a distinguishing factor between Muslims and disbelievers.

Hazrat Usman Accepts Islam

Hazrat Usman accepted Islam instantly when his friend Hazrat Abu Bakr invited him to Islam.

The First Child to Accept Islam

Hazrat Ali was the first among children to embrace Islam; he was at that time only ten years old.

Qualities of Hazrat Umar

Hazrat Umar's justice and discipline are greatly liked. He ruled with justice, granted scholarships to the poor, and served Islam and the Muslims for ten and a half years. He is a role model for Muslim leaders who want to rule with justice.

The Life of Hazrat Ali

Hazrat Ali was the son of Hazrat Abu Talib, the uncle of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him). From his early childhood he lived with Rasoolullah and was brought up in his care. He was the first child to embrace Islam, at the age of ten. He wrote letters and treaties for Rasoolullah, and he was a very courageous man, known as Asadullah, the Lion of Allah. After the martyrdom of Hazrat Usman, he became the fourth caliph of Islam and performed his duties for almost five years.

The Title 'Siddique'

Siddique means the truthful one. Hazrat Abu Bakr was given this title because he was a man of good habits who always spoke the truth and at once confirmed whatever Rasoolullah said. The lesson text states the title and his good habits; the meaning of the title is the standard reason for it.

Zun-Noorain — Holder of Two Lights

Hazrat Usman married two of Hazrat Muhammad's daughters, both at different times. For this he became known as Zun-Noorain, meaning holder of two lights.

Hazrat Ali's Age

Hazrat Ali accepted Islam at the age of ten years.

Digraphs and Trigraphs

A digraph is a group of two letters that makes a single sound; a trigraph is a group of three letters that makes a single sound.

  • ch: chick, chair
  • wh: wheel, what
  • igh: fight, night
  • tch: watch, catch

Silent Letters

Silent letters are spelt in words but not pronounced.

  • lamb — silent b
  • bike — silent e
  • know — silent k
  • write — silent w
  • talk — silent l

The Caliphs — Completed Sentences

  • The first caliph of Islam was Hazrat Abu Bakr.
  • Hazrat Abu Bakr was a friend of Rasoolullah.
  • Hazrat Usman was a very rich trader.
  • Hazrat Ali was the first among children to accept Islam.
  • Hazrat Umar was the second caliph of Islam.

Personality Traits of the Caliphs

  • Hazrat Abu Bakr: kind-hearted, loving, generous.
  • Hazrat Umar: just, disciplined, brave, a good administrator.
  • Hazrat Usman: pious, generous (Ghani), modest.
  • Hazrat Ali: courageous (Asadullah), loyal, wise.

mcqs.why: The lesson tells us that Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique was the first among men to embrace Islam.

mcqs.why: Al-Farooq means the one who distinguishes between the right and the wrong; Rasoolullah (peace be upon him) gave this title to Hazrat Umar.

mcqs.q: At what age did Hazrat Ali accept Islam?
mcqs.why: Hazrat Ali was the first among children to embrace Islam, and at that time he was only ten years old.

options: He was a very rich trader
He granted scholarships to the poor
He married two daughters of Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) at different times
mcqs.why: Hazrat Usman married two of Hazrat Muhammad's (peace be upon him) daughters, both at different times, so he became known as Zun-Noorain, holder of two lights.

mcqs.q: What does 'Siddique' mean?
mcqs.why: Siddique means the truthful one; Hazrat Abu Bakr got this title because he always spoke the truth and at once confirmed whatever Rasoolullah (peace be upon him) said.

mcqs.why: The lesson says Hazrat Umar ruled with justice and served Islam and the Muslims for ten and a half years.

mcqs.q: In the word 'lamb', which letter is silent?
mcqs.why: In 'lamb' the letter b is not pronounced, so b is the silent letter; the notes list lamb — silent b.

mcqs.q: Which group of letters is a trigraph?
mcqs.why: A trigraph is a group of three letters making a single sound; 'igh' in fight and night is a trigraph, while ch and wh are digraphs of two letters.

Words Beginning with Vowel Sounds

There are five vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in the English alphabet.

  • Words beginning with vowel sounds: envelope, octopus, umpire, apricot.
  • Sister, cloud and trophy begin with consonant sounds.

Greetings Dialogue

Sadia: Assalamu Alaikum! Ayaan: Wa Alaikum Assalaam. Sadia: How are you? Ayaan: I am fine. Thank you! Ayaan: Are you going to the playground? Sadia: Yes, I am. And you? Ayaan: Yes, me too. Can we play together? Sadia: Yes, we can.

Speaking Practice

Students work in pairs and express their willingness or unwillingness to participate in a debate competition.

mcqs.why: The speaking practice asks students to work in pairs and express their willingness or unwillingness to participate in a debate competition.

lessons.title: Language Focus and Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • affection — feelings of love
  • distinguish — to recognise the difference
  • generous — open-handed
  • treaties — a formal agreement between two or more countries
  • martyr — the person who dies for religion or patriotism

Naming, Action and Describing Words

  • Naming words: tree, boy, butterfly.
  • Action words: walking, playing, sitting.
  • Describing words: green, colourful, happy.

Dictionary Work

Words in a dictionary are arranged in alphabetical order.

  • amazing (a-maz-ing), adjective — causing great surprise or wonder
  • ambassador (am-bas-sa-dor), noun — a diplomat sent by a state as its permanent representative in a foreign country
  • ambiguity (am-bi-gu-i-ty), noun — a word or statement that can be understood in more than one way

Spelling

The completed words are: caliphate, enemies, leader, husband, recite.

Countable and Uncountable Nouns

Countable nouns are things we can count, with singular and plural forms. Uncountable nouns are things we cannot count, with no plural forms.

  • Countable nouns: ball, girl, doll, flower, butterfly.
  • Uncountable nouns: water, weather, furniture, air, fun.
  • From the lesson passage: countable — flowers, swings, butterflies; uncountable — weather, air, fun.

Articles — a, an and the

  • The man who wrote this book is famous.
  • There is a bag on the table.
  • She has an old watch.
  • He is drinking a glass of milk.
  • Kalsoom is a pilot.
  • There is an airport in my city.
  • Do you know where I left the car keys?

A is used with words starting with consonant sounds; an is used with words starting with vowel sounds; the is used when we know there is only one of a particular thing or person.

Adjectives

  • Size: large, tiny.
  • Quality: soft, kind.
  • Colour: pink, blue.
  • Shape: triangle, square.
  • Origin: Pakistani, Punjabi.
  • Quantity: four, much.

Capitalisation

  • Peshawar, Lahore, Quetta and Karachi are the most famous cities of Pakistan.
  • The teacher asked Danish to read the lesson.
  • Mano is a naughty cat.
  • We cannot go to Islamabad on this Friday.
  • Asif lives in Gilgit.

Capitalise the initial letter of each sentence and the initial letter of a proper noun.

Multi-Syllable Words

A word which carries more than one syllable is called a multi-syllable word.

grand-fa-ther, com-pan-ions, bal-loon, rain-bow, ba-na-na, e-le-phant, class-room, af-ter-noon, sis-ter, tea-cher, lead-er-ship, op-po-nent.

More multi-syllable words with a dot between syllables: pock-et, pas-ta, win-dow, gar-den, pic-ture, but-ter-fly, morn-ing, sum-mer.

Replacing Words and Phrases

  • His uncle has a house like Faisal's.
  • I love my siblings.
  • He bought costly dresses.
  • Allah is the Creator of everything.

Creative Writing

Students write a paragraph about Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) in their own words, using correct punctuation and spelling, following this mind map:

  • Date of birth and place
  • Personality traits
  • Date of death
  • Career
  • Achievements
  • Family

mcqs.why: Treaties are formal agreements between two or more countries; Hazrat Ali wrote letters and treaties for Rasoolullah (peace be upon him).

mcqs.why: Walking is an action word; tree and butterfly are naming words, and green is a describing word.

mcqs.q: How are words arranged in a dictionary?
mcqs.why: Words in a dictionary are arranged in alphabetical order, which helps us find a word quickly.

mcqs.why: Water cannot be counted and has no plural form, so it is an uncountable noun; ball, doll and flower are countable.

mcqs.why: 'Old' begins with a vowel sound, so we use 'an' before it: 'She has an old watch.'

mcqs.why: Large shows size; soft shows quality, pink shows colour, and Pakistani shows origin.

mcqs.why: In the vocabulary list of this lesson, 'affection' means feelings of love.

lessons.title: The Lesson: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Life Cycle of a Butterfly

The life cycle of a butterfly has four stages: egg, caterpillar (larva), pupa (chrysalis) and butterfly.

Other insects: honeybee, ladybird, ant, mosquito, grasshopper.

About the Caterpillar

The poem is about a caterpillar. A caterpillar is the larva of a butterfly or moth; it is brown and furry, it walks to a shady leaf or stalk, spins a cocoon, and in the end becomes a butterfly.

The Poem

Brown and furry, / Caterpillar in a hurry, / Take your walk / To the shady leaf, or stalk, / Or what not, / Which may be the chosen spot. / No toad spy you, / Hovering bird of prey pass by you; / Spin and die, / To live again a butterfly. — Christina Rossetti

About the Caterpillar

The colour of a caterpillar is brown (and furry).

Liking the Poem

The poem is liked because it describes the caterpillar in a beautiful way and tells how it becomes a butterfly in the end.

Seeing a Caterpillar

A brown, furry caterpillar was once seen on a leaf in a garden. It was walking slowly towards a shady leaf. Later it would spin a cocoon and become a butterfly.

Where the Caterpillar Goes

The caterpillar is going to the shady leaf, or stalk — the chosen spot.

What the Caterpillar Becomes

The caterpillar becomes a butterfly: spin and die, to live again a butterfly.

Toads and Birds of Prey

Toads and birds of prey eat caterpillars. The poem warns the caterpillar: 'No toad spy you, hovering bird of prey pass by you.'

Mahnoor's Charts

One day Mahnoor was playing in a park with her friends. She noticed that people were plucking flowers, killing insects and making the park dirty. She was so upset. She wanted to save insects and the environment but could not think of any idea. She went to her mother to ask for help. Her mother told her to make a colourful chart about importance of plants, trees, insects and birds. It was indeed a very good idea to seek everyone's attention. Her friends, Amna and Salma, helped her too. They made many charts together and put them up all over the garden. They also gave the charts to their neighbours.

Key Facts

  • The poem 'Caterpillar' was written by Christina Rossetti.
  • A caterpillar is an insect.
  • The caterpillar is walking to the shady leaf.
  • At the end, the caterpillar becomes a butterfly.

The Honeybee

  • Honeybees live in hives and work together in groups.
  • They make honey from the nectar of flowers.
  • They pollinate flowers, which helps plants make fruit and seeds.
  • A honeybee has a sting which it uses to protect its hive.

options: Make a colourful chart about the importance of plants, trees, insects and birds
mcqs.why: Her mother told her to make a colourful chart about the importance of plants, trees, insects and birds to seek everyone's attention.

mcqs.why: Her friends Amna and Salma helped her; they made many charts together and put them up all over the garden.

mcqs.why: Honeybees live in hives, work together in groups and make honey from the nectar of flowers.

  • thumb — silent b
  • honest — silent h
  • autumn — silent n
  • knee — silent k
  • wrap — silent w

  • when — silent h

More words: sign (g), calm (l), comb (b), hour (h), column (n), knife (k), write (w), listen (t).

Caterpillar: Good morning, Butterfly! How are you? Butterfly: Good morning! I am fine. Thank you. Caterpillar: Meet my friend, Ladybird. Butterfly: Good to meet you, Ladybird. lessons.title: Language Focus and Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • furry — covered with fur
  • stalk — the main stem of a plant
  • hover — to stay in the air at one place
  • toad — a small animal like a frog but with drier and less smooth skin
  • spy — to observe silently

Rhyming Words

A little seed for me to sow, / A little soil to grow, / A little hole, a little pat, / A little wish, and that, / A little sun, a little shower, / A little while, and then, a flower.

Writing Practice

Students create a poem of their own using the pairs of rhyming words way/day and trees/bees.

Expressing Likes, Needs and Feelings

Anum: Did you like the poem about the life cycle of a caterpillar? Iqra: Yes, I did. It was good. Anum: Do you like reading scientific magazines and articles? Iqra: No, I don't. But I prefer to read different funny story books. Adnan: Hi, Hamza, you look so excited. What's the matter? Hamza: Yes, I'm very happy because I am going to visit my family. Adnan: Wow! That's great! Could I borrow your bag? I want to put my stuff in it. Hamza: Sure, you can. Adnan: Thank you!

Likes and dislikes are expressed with phrases such as 'Yes, I did. It was good.' and 'No, I don't. But I prefer...'; a need is expressed with 'Could I borrow your bag?'

Spelling

The completed words are: stalk, caterpillar, hover, spin, prey. Stalk, hover, spin and prey are all words of this unit.

Collective Nouns

A collective noun refers to a group of people or things, e.g. a crowd of people, a bouquet of flowers, a flock of butterflies, a swarm of bees, a hive of bees.

  • A team of players won the match.
  • A herd of deer ran across the field.
  • A gang of robbers was caught by the police.
  • A cluster of grapes hung from the vine.
  • A pride of lions rested under the tree.

Articles 'a' and 'an'

  • an honest girl
  • a wrapper
  • a knife
  • an hour

Some words have initial consonants which are not pronounced, e.g. 'w' in write, 'k' in kneel, 'h' in honest. We put a or an with those words by focusing on the second letter: honest — 'o' is a vowel, so 'an'; knife — 'n' is a consonant, so 'a'.

Aqsa brought an apple, an orange and a sandwich for lunch today. She cut the fruits with a knife. They were from her own garden. The vegetables in her garden are always very fresh. She always shares her lunch with her friends.

Adjectives of Origin

  • Shazia likes to eat Australian apples.
  • He has bought a new Italian car.
  • Pakistani culture is a diverse culture.
  • Maha wants to buy a beautiful Multani dress.
  • I have a British friend.
  • She speaks Spanish.
  • Pakistani mangoes are famous.
  • He is a Canadian citizen.
  • American films are popular all over the world.

Capitalisation

Mohsin lives in Faisalabad. Sadia, Maha and Mohsin are my best friends. Bunny is Mohsin's pet rabbit. Mr Sohail is Mohsin's father. He is a banker.

The Life Cycle of a Butterfly — Model Paragraph

The life cycle of a butterfly has four stages. First, the butterfly lays eggs on a leaf. Then the eggs hatch and a caterpillar comes out. The caterpillar eats leaves and grows bigger, but it must hide from toads and birds. After some time it spins a cocoon and becomes a pupa. At last, a beautiful butterfly comes out of the cocoon because nature has changed it completely.

The main idea of a paragraph is called a topic sentence. Other sentences in a paragraph support the topic sentence. These are called supporting details.

Creative Writing

Students write a paragraph on 'Saving Earth' in their own words.

options: A small animal like a frog
The main stem of a plant
To stay in the air at one place
mcqs.why: In the vocabulary list, 'stalk' means the main stem of a plant.

mcqs.why: A collective noun refers to a group; 'a swarm of bees' names a group, like a flock of butterflies or a bouquet of flowers.

mcqs.why: Team and herd are collective nouns because they refer to groups of people or animals.

mcqs.why: The h in 'honest' is silent, so the word begins with the vowel sound 'o' and takes 'an': an honest girl.

mcqs.why: Australian tells where the apples come from, so it is an adjective of origin, like Italian, Pakistani and British.

mcqs.why: Lahore is the name of a particular city, so it is a proper noun and is written with a capital letter. City, rabbit and garden are common nouns.

mcqs.q: The main idea of a paragraph is called its:
mcqs.why: The main idea of a paragraph is called a topic sentence; the other sentences, called supporting details, support it.

mcqs.q: What is the second stage of a butterfly's life cycle?
mcqs.why: The four stages in order are: egg, caterpillar (larva), pupa (chrysalis) and butterfly, so the caterpillar is the second stage.

lessons.title: The Lesson: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Recycling Fruit and Vegetable Peels

Fruit and vegetable peels can be put in a hole and left for some time; organic components are formed which are added to the soil as organic fertilizer to help plants grow.

Families can be taught to recycle waste things — for example, use peels for fertilizer and reuse paper, plastic and glass — instead of throwing them away.

The Lesson Text

We have all eaten chocolate but not many of us know where it comes from or how it is made. Historians say chocolate has been around for almost 2000 years. In ancient times, chocolate was a symbol of wealth as only the rich could afford it. Chocolate came from Central and South America to Spain in the 1500s through Spanish explorers who brought it back with them. It became very popular and soon spread throughout Europe. Chocolate comes from cocoa trees in its raw form. It is very surprising that the flowers of a cocoa tree grow on the trunk of the tree, not on its branches. These flowers grow throughout the year. When the fruit is ripe, large reddish pods hang all over the tree. Each pod contains 20 to 40 beans. It takes the pod about six months to ripen. After that, the pods are collected into heaps and then split open to remove the beans. First of all, the beans are heated or placed in the hot sun to dry. Then they are sent to factories. Chocolate beans are cleaned before they are roasted in a big oven. Next the shells are removed. The nibs are roasted and mixed with sugar and made into a paste. Dried milk and some flavours are added to the mixture. This mixture is then poured into big trays. A granite roller is pushed in each tray for several days. The chocolate now becomes a fine liquid. Finally, this liquid is left to harden. This is how chocolate is made. Chocolate is no doubt a good source of vitamins and minerals, but eating too much chocolate is not a good habit. We must remember to always brush our teeth after eating chocolate.

Who Invented Chocolate

No single inventor is named in the lesson. Chocolate came from Central and South America and was brought to Spain in the 1500s by Spanish explorers; it then spread throughout Europe. The lesson text names no inventor — the history follows the lesson's own account.

Too Much Chocolate

Eating too much chocolate is not a good habit: it is bad for health and for teeth, so we must always brush our teeth after eating chocolate.

An Invention Idea

A machine that cleans a room by itself would make life easier, giving more time to study and play.

Where Cocoa Flowers Grow

The cocoa flowers grow on the trunk of the tree, not on its branches.

Beans in a Pod

Each pod contains 20 to 40 beans.

Nibs

Nibs are the cocoa beans after their shells have been removed; they are roasted and mixed with sugar and made into a paste.

Joining Words

Joining words are words connecting one sentence to another or one paragraph to the next paragraph. Joining words in the lesson: First of all, Then, Next, Finally and After that.

Pie Chart — Favourite Food

  • The most favourite food item is Chocolate.
  • 35 children like chocolate.

Vocabulary

Anagrams

An anagram is a word that is made by re-arranging the letters of another word in a different order.

  • thing → night
  • dusty → study
  • trap → part
  • race → care
  • keen → knee
  • teach → cheat
  • heart → earth
  • lake → kale

Spelling

The completed words are: granite, delicious, solidify, minerals, contains.

Regular and Irregular Nouns

  • goose → geese
  • flower → flowers
  • man → men
  • apple → apples
  • watch → watches

Regular nouns form their plural by adding 's' or 'es' to the end: chocolate → chocolates, plant → plants, dish → dishes. Irregular nouns do not follow any particular pattern: tooth → teeth, ox → oxen, foot → feet.

Action Verbs

  • heated — The beans are heated in the sun.
  • cleaned — The workers cleaned the beans.
  • roasted — The beans are roasted in a big oven.
  • removed — The shells are removed.
  • mixed — The nibs are mixed with sugar.

Prepositions of Position

  • The rabbit is under the bed.
  • Our school is between the park and the market.
  • A lamp hung over the table.
  • The cat climbed up the tree.
  • I saw people around the garden.

Prepositions of position indicate where something is, for example: around, up, between, under, over, below.

Capitalisation and Punctuation

  • July comes after June.
  • What is Shazia doing?
  • They buy nuts every Sunday.
  • I live in Pakistan.

Sentences always begin with a capital letter. The names of people, pets, places and things always start with a capital letter. The names of days of the week and months also start with capital letters.

Method: Firstly, melt the chocolate bar. Secondly, pour the milk into two glasses. Then, add the melted chocolate and one teaspoon of sugar to the milk. Finally, stir well and serve.

lessons.title: The Lesson: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Our National Heroes

The children keeping their neighbourhood clean and the people helping each other during the pandemic are our national heroes. They need to be encouraged and honoured. We can show love for the country by keeping our surroundings clean, helping others, obeying the law and working honestly for Pakistan.

The Lesson Text

Finally, the day came when we took the school bus to go for our historical trip to Pakistan Army Museum, Lahore. My close friend and classmate, Tashif, brought his diary along with him. It was his hobby to collect pictures and information about Pakistan Army as his uncle was an army officer. I, too, eagerly wanted to know more about those great heroes who sacrificed their lives for the country. Since that day both of us had been waiting impatiently to meet those eleven heroes from the armed forces who laid down their lives to guard the sacred land of Pakistan. We arrived at the museum at around 10 a.m. There were many big galleries, huge slabs and walls. These galleries and slabs had different names: Rebirth of a Nation, the Quaid and the Armed Forces, Shuhada Corner, Nishan-e-Haider Gallery, Life at Siachen, Kashmir Corner, etc. On getting inside the museum building, I first saw four captured Indian tanks. A brief history of the encounters in which these Indian tanks were captured was displayed near them. One of the galleries was named 'Rebirth of the Nation'. I was surprised to see life-size portraits of the Quaid-e-Azam addressing the constituent assembly of Pakistan on August 11, 1947. This gallery was telling a story of struggle for freedom through paintings, photographs and brief information. Finally I went to the 'Nishan-e-Haider Gallery'. Here, I came to know about the Nishan-e-Haider and its value. Our teacher told us that this highest military award is awarded to those soldiers and officers of the armed forces who sacrifice their lives for their country in an extraordinary act of bravery. Nishan-e-Haider means 'Mark of the Lion'. The eleven holders: 1948 Captain Muhammad Sarwar; 1948 Naik Saif Ali Janjua; 1958 Major Tufail Muhammad; 1965 Major Raja Aziz Bhatti; 1971 Major Muhammad Akram; 1971 Major Shabbir Sharif; 1971 Sawar Muhammad Hussain; 1971 Pilot Officer Rashid Minhas; 1971 Lance Naik Muhammad Mahfuz; 1999 Captain Karnal Sher Khan; 1999 Havildar Lalak Jan. I explored the museum with my classmates for more than three hours. The army museum was worth visiting. I will surely visit it with my family sometime again.

The Nishan-e-Haider Holders

Eleven soldiers have been awarded the Nishan-e-Haider. Two of them are Captain Muhammad Sarwar and Major Raja Aziz Bhatti.

Recipients of the Nishan-e-Haider

The Nishan-e-Haider is awarded to soldiers and officers of the armed forces who sacrifice their lives for their country in an extraordinary act of bravery.

About the Nishan-e-Haider

Nishan-e-Haider is the highest military award of Pakistan. It means 'Mark of the Lion'. It is awarded to soldiers and officers who sacrifice their lives for their country in an extraordinary act of bravery. Since 1947, eleven men from the armed forces have won this award. Their pictures in the Nishan-e-Haider Gallery made us so proud — those were our heroes.

Soldiers as National Heroes

Soldiers are our national heroes because they guard our sacred land, protect our motherland, and sacrifice their lives for the country. They show bravery, discipline and love for Pakistan.

Galleries of the Museum

Shuhada Corner (and the Nishan-e-Haider Gallery) told us about martyrs.

Rebirth of the Nation Gallery

Life-size portraits of the Quaid-e-Azam addressing the constituent assembly of Pakistan on August 11, 1947, and the story of the struggle for freedom through paintings, photographs and brief information were displayed in the 'Rebirth of the Nation'.

Learning from a Museum Visit

By visiting a museum we learn about our history, our heroes and their sacrifices. We gain a treasure trove of knowledge and feel proud of our country.

  • Life history

  • Nishan-e-Haider is the highest military award in Pakistan.

  • There are eleven great soldiers from the armed forces who received the Nishan-e-Haider.

lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • sacrifice — to lay down life for a noble cause
  • impatient — restless
  • martyr — a person who sacrifices his life for a noble cause
  • struggle — to try hard to do or achieve something
  • sacred — to treat someone with great respect
  • capture — to take control

Changing Parts of Speech

  • admire (verb) — admiration (noun), admirable (adjective)
  • selection (noun) — select (verb), selective (adjective)
  • beautiful (adjective) — beauty (noun), beautify (verb)

Suffixes '-ly', '-ion', '-ing', etc. are used to convert verbs to nouns and adjectives. Examples: play → player, played, playful; sad → sadness, sadden; cooperate → cooperation, cooperative.

Synonyms and Antonyms

  • brave — synonym: courageous; antonym: coward
  • battle — synonym: war; antonym: peace
  • intelligent — synonym: bright; antonym: stupid
  • victorious — synonym: successful; antonym: defeated
  • happy — synonym: joyful; antonym: sad
  • big — synonym: large; antonym: small
  • fast — synonym: quick; antonym: slow
  • kind — synonym: gentle; antonym: cruel
  • strong — synonym: powerful; antonym: weak

Learning to Spell

The correct spellings are smile, speech, learn, faith, moment, period.

Nouns with No Change in the Plural

The sheep are grazing in the field. Sana has long hair. I saw deer in the forest.

Some nouns have an unchanged plural form.

Helping Verbs

Ali is climbing the tree. Soldiers are fighting bravely. The boys did not finish their work. Tashif's uncle had told us different stories about Pakistani soldiers. She has bought a new dress. I am reading a book. We have completed our homework.

Helping verbs help the main verb in a sentence, for example: is, are, am, has, have, had, do, does, did.

Prepositions of Time

We have lunch at noon. I have a meeting at 9 a.m. They go to the beach in summer. They went for a walk in the morning. The test is on Wednesday. What did you do on Eid last year?

Prepositions of time introduce time, for example a date, days of the week, etc.

Degrees of Regular Adjectives

  • Positive (P) — thin, dark, wild, smart
  • Comparative (C) — softer, brighter, smaller
  • Superlative (S) — busiest, biggest, greatest

Regular adjectives take 'er' and 'est' to make comparative and superlative adjectives. Comparative adjectives compare two things using 'than'. Superlative adjectives compare two or more things. Examples: heavy → heavier → heaviest; large → larger → largest; lucky → luckier → luckiest; old → older → oldest.

Degrees of Regular Adjectives

The garden is lovely. My bag is smaller than yours. He is the greatest player in our team.

Capitalisation

Tashif is reading a book 'How to Keep the Earth Safe'. The title of my favourite story is 'Honesty is the Best Policy'. 'The Dove and the Ant' is an interesting story.

The names of holidays, special events and groups start with capital letters: Independence Day of Pakistan is celebrated on August 14. Pakistanis are brave people. They had arranged a speech competition on Defence Day. Book titles are capitalised: English Textbook for Grade 5, Two Little Kittens, Special Person.

A Descriptive Paragraph

Nishan-e-Haider is the highest military award of Pakistan. The meaning of 'Nishan-e-Haider' is 'Mark of the Lion'. Usually, it is made from gun metal captured from the enemy. It is composed of 88 percent of copper, 10 percent tin and 2 percent zinc. Since 1947, eleven men from the armed forces have won this award. It is awarded to the members of the armed forces for their heroic acts in dangerous situations and for sacrificing their lives.

A descriptive paragraph describes a particular situation, person, place or thing.

Writing Practice

lessons.title: The Lesson: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Trees and the Environment

Cutting a tree is not a right act. If trees are cut for wood and fuel, the environment will be damaged — there will be less oxygen, less shelter for birds and animals, more heat and more pollution. Trees give us oxygen, shade, shelter, fruits, wood and a clean, healthy environment.

The picture shows a tree begging: 'Please, don't kill me! I give you oxygen and shelter.'

The Poem

Thank You, Lord, by Mary Fairchild: Lord, in the morning I start each day
By taking a moment to bow and pray.
I start with thanks, and then give praise
For all your kind and loving ways.
Today if sunshine turns to rain,
If a dark cloud brings some pain,
I won't doubt or hide in fear
For you, my God, are always near.
I will travel where you lead;
I will help my friends in need.
Where you send me, I will go;
With your help, I'll learn and grow.
Hold my family in your hands
As we follow your commands
And I will keep you close in sight
Until I crawl in bed tonight.

How the Poet Starts Her Day

The poet starts her day by taking a moment to bow and pray; she starts with thanks, and then gives praise.

Helping Friends

We should help our friends in need, travel where we are led, and follow good commands — helping friends is part of thanking God.

Thanking Allah (SWT)

We thank Allah (SWT) for His blessings — for all His kind and loving ways, for our family, health, food and everything He has given us.

The Poet in Difficult Times

In her difficult times, the poet will not doubt or hide in fear, for God is always near.

The Poet's Resolve

The poet will keep God close in sight, travel where He leads, help her friends in need, and follow His commands until she crawls in bed tonight.

Thanking Allah (SWT)

We thank Allah (SWT) by praying, by starting our day with thanks and praise, by obeying His commands and by helping others.

Telling the Time

7:15 is read as 'quarter past seven'. 10:45 is read as 'quarter to eleven'.

Telling the Time

First clock: 4:15 — quarter past four. Second clock: 5:45 — quarter to six.

Key Facts

  • 'Thank you, Lord' is a poem by Mary Fairchild.
  • The poet is talking to God.
  • The poet starts her day in the morning.
  • The poet will help her friends in need.

Analytical Reading

lessons.notes_html:
Consonant Clusters

  • Initial consonant clusters — split (spl-), script (scr-), strong (str-)
  • Final consonant clusters — gulps (-lps), pumps (-mps), attempts (-pts)

A consonant cluster is a group of two or three consonants in a word. Each consonant retains its sound when we say the word. Initial: str- strip, string, straight; scr- scream, screw, scrap; spl- splash, split, splendid. Final: -pts accepts, adopts, interrupts; -lps helps, scalps, pulps; -mps lamps, stamps, jumps.

Speaking Practice

Mahira: Assalaamu Alaikum!

Aqsa: Wa Alaikum Assalaam!

Mahira: Did you enjoy the visit to Faisal Masjid?

Aqsa: Yes, I enjoyed it. I really liked the beautiful architecture and the big prayer room. What do you say?

Mahira: Yes, I liked it too. Usually I don't like big light globes but I like the ones in the Faisal Masjid. They are very beautiful and attractive.

Aqsa: Yes, you are right. They look very attractive.

Classroom Discussion

Activity: Hold a classroom discussion and express your views on your favourite places to visit.

lessons.title: Language Focus and Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • praise — to say nice things about somebody
  • hide — to put or keep out of sight
  • fear — be afraid of
  • command — an order given to a person
  • crawl — an act of moving on your hands and knees

Homophones

  • deer — dear: My dear friend came to my house.
  • night — knight: The knight was very brave.
  • sea — see: I can see the sea from here.
  • rein — rain: It will rain today.

Homophones are words that sound the same but have different meanings and spellings. Examples: son/sun, steel/steal, prey/pray, lessen/lesson.

Learning to Spell

The correct spellings are cloud, morning, family, praise, crawl.

Gender Nouns

  • Masculine — king, prince, brother
  • Feminine — actress, queen, lioness
  • Neuter — phone, flower, crayons

Nouns that name male creatures have the masculine gender. Nouns that name female creatures have the feminine gender. Nouns that name non-living things have the neuter gender. Examples: Masculine: husband, father, uncle, tiger. Feminine: wife, mother, aunt, tigress. Neuter: knife, chair, bag, pencil.

Changing Gender

My nephew has a pet cat named Kitty. The waitress is waiting for the order. She is our headmistress. The tiger is running in the jungle. My uncle will come tomorrow.

'Be', 'Do' and 'Have' as Helping Verbs

  • The cows are (helping verb) not grazing (main verb) in the fields.
  • She has (helping verb) sewn (main verb) her dress.
  • We did (helping verb) not watch (main verb) the news channel.
  • He had (helping verb) not gone (main verb) yet.
  • He is (helping verb) drinking (main verb) mango juice.

'Be', 'do' and 'have' are helping verbs when they are used with another verb in a sentence. 'Be', 'do' and 'have' are main verbs when they are used alone in a sentence. We use 'not' with be, do and have when they are used as helping verbs in negative sentences. Examples: She is not playing with the doll. They are not going to Lahore. He was not on leave. We have not received the parcel. They were not tired. She has not completed her tasks.

Apostrophe and Exclamation Mark

My brother's car. Oh! I forgot your name. Please help me! I am not making my breakfast. Wow! What a beautiful scene!

An exclamation mark (!) is used to express sudden feelings or emotions. An apostrophe (') is used to show possession. Examples: The customers' trolleys. Student's notebook. Hurrah! We have won the match! My daughter's hat. What an amazing car!

Blessings of Allah (SWT)

  • Topic sentence — Allah (SWT) has given us countless blessings.
  • Supporting detail 1 — eyes to see, ears to hear, hands to work
  • Supporting detail 2 — food, water, family and a beautiful world to live in
  • Conclusion — We should thank Allah (SWT) for His blessings every day.

Write a paragraph on 'Blessings of Allah (SWT)' using the information filled in this mind map.

The Five Senses

  • Sight (eyes) — we see the world
  • Hearing (ears) — we hear sounds
  • Smell (nose) — we smell food and flowers
  • Taste (tongue) — we taste food
  • Touch (skin) — we feel hot, cold, soft and rough

Activity: Write a paragraph about the five senses of the human body and their functions in daily life, using these points.

mcqs.why: An apostrophe (') is used to show possession, as in 'My brother's car' and 'My daughter's hat'; the exclamation mark shows sudden feelings.

mcqs.why: The five senses are sight (eyes), hearing (ears), smell (nose), taste (tongue) and touch (skin).

lessons.title: The Lesson: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Faraz Is Special

Faraz is sad because he thinks he is not like others.

He does not need to be disappointed.

Allah (SWT) made him special because he is a Math genius.

Everyone is special in his or her own way.

In the picture, Ayesha asks Faraz what made him so sad, and Faraz says that he is not like others.

Ayesha tells him that he is special, because Allah (SWT) made him special as a Math genius.

The Lesson Text

One evening, Rehan found his best friend, Sa'ad, sitting alone on a bench in a park. He seemed really upset. Rehan asked Sa'ad what made him so sad and gloomy. Sa'ad said, 'I am feeling guilty about my rude behaviour.' Rehan exclaimed, 'I don't understand. Can you please explain?' Sa'ad said, 'I have been rude to one of my classmates who limped while walking. I often made fun of him for that. My rudeness grew with time. Being the captain of the team, I was shocked to know that Faraz had been selected as a wicketkeeper. I completely ignored his good performance and was unkind to him because of his physical issue. He added, 'Faraz was so depressed by my rude behaviour that he left school. Now, I am feeling so ashamed at being rude to him. I will never be able to forgive myself.' Rehan told him that it was not too late. He told Sa'ad to go to Faraz's house and say sorry for his wrong attitude. Sa'ad agreed soon and they both went to Faraz's house. Faraz was pleased to see them. Sa'ad apologised to him for his rudeness. Faraz was a good boy. He forgave and hugged him at once. They became good friends.

Sa'ad's Sadness

Sa'ad was feeling guilty about his rude behaviour towards Faraz.

Feeling Guilty

A person can feel bad after being rude to a friend.

He or she feels guilty afterwards and says sorry, just like Sa'ad did.

Students give their own answer.

Forgiving Others

A person in Faraz's place would feel sad and hurt if someone made fun of him or her.

He or she would forgive the person who apologised sincerely, just as Faraz did.

Treating Differently-Abled People

We should treat a differently-abled person with respect, kindness and love.

We should never be rude to a differently-abled person and never make fun of him or her.

A differently-abled person should be helped, spoken to politely, included in games and work, and valued for his or her special abilities.

Sa'ad's Sadness

Sa'ad was sitting sad because he was feeling guilty about his rude behaviour towards Faraz.

Why Faraz Left School

Faraz was so depressed by Sa'ad's rude behaviour that he left school.

Sa'ad had made fun of him for limping while walking, ignored his good performance and was unkind to him because of his physical issue.

Faraz Forgives Sa'ad

Faraz was a good boy.

He forgave Sa'ad and hugged him at once, and they became good friends.

Inflectional Endings

Inflectional endings are a letter or a group of letters added to the end of a word to change the form of the word.

  • -s — books, cats
  • -es — boxes, watches
  • -ed — played, walked
  • -ing — reading, playing

I have many books.

She watches cartoons.

We played cricket yesterday.

They are reading English.

Faraz goes to the library every day.

My teacher never complains about my behaviour.

Faraz listened to his teacher carefully.

Ali is going to buy fruit from the market.

Faraz and Sa'ad started practising for the final match.

Compound Words

  • butterfly — butter + fly
  • rainbow — rain + bow

Two words combine to make a compound word.

Each word has its own meaning, but when we join them, they give a single new meaning.

Compound Words

  • sunflower — sun + flower
  • football — foot + ball
  • ladybird — lady + bird
  • butterfly — butter + fly

Key Facts from the Lesson

  • Rehan is the best friend of Sa'ad.
  • Sa'ad was feeling guilty at his rude behaviour.
  • Faraz limped while walking.
  • Faraz was selected as wicketkeeper of the cricket team.
  • Sa'ad said sorry to Faraz for his bad behaviour.

Accessibility Symbols

  • Eye symbol (with slash) — Facilities for the visually impaired
  • Ear symbol (with T) — Facilities for the hard of hearing
  • Wheelchair with standing person — Accessible Toilet
  • Person pushing a wheelchair up a ramp — Ramped Access

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
Sounds of 'the'

  • the (thee) before a vowel sound — the orange, the apples, the umbrellas, the owner
  • the (thuh) before a consonant sound — the bottles, the match, the file, the house

When 'the' comes before a vowel sound, it is pronounced as 'thee', but when it comes before a consonant sound, it is pronounced as 'thuh'.

Asking to Borrow and Asking for Help

Faraz: May I borrow your helmet? I need it for tomorrow's match.

Sa'ad: Of course, but please try to return it soon.

Faraz: Sure, thank you.

Asma: Could you please help me complete my new painting?

Samra: Yes, sure. But I think you should first try it yourself.

Asma: You are right. I should try it at least once.

Samra: I am sure you can do it.

Asma: Thank you!

Speaking Practice

Practise asking a friend to let you use his or her storybook, and also practise seeking permission to use different things that belong to your friend, such as a spare pencil or a sharpener.

lessons.title: Language Focus and Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Analytical Reading

Read the information about any differently-abled person on the internet and make a list of five qualities he or she has.

Vocabulary

  • gloomy — sad
  • rude — showing lack of respect
  • depressed — unhappy
  • guilty — feeling ashamed
  • apologise — to say sorry

Compound Words

  • butterfly — butter + fly
  • rainbow — rain + bow
  • sunflower — sun + flower
  • football — foot + ball

Learning to Spell

The complete words are depressed, limp, guilty, hug and bench.

Common and Proper Nouns

  • Common nouns — teacher, people, world
  • Proper nouns — Helen Keller, Anne Sullivan, Braille

Common nouns are the names of people, places, animals or things in general, for example: book, cat, woman.

Proper nouns are the names of particular persons, places, animals or things, and they always start with a capital letter, for example: Azam, Lahore.

We spent last week in Nathia Gali.

We visited the Mukeshpuri Top and the National Park.

It was my first visit to a hill station and I enjoyed it a lot.

'Be', 'Do' and 'Have' as Verbs

  • As helping verbs — I am reading a story. We had bought a house. You are going to school. He has written a story. They have decided to go out. Did she pass her exam?
  • As main verbs — I am a student. We had a house. You are late. He has two siblings. They have a bicycle. He did a great job.

'Be', 'do' and 'have' are helping verbs when they are used with another verb in a sentence.

'Be', 'do' and 'have' are main verbs when they are used alone in a sentence.

Punctuation

  • Hurrah! We won the match.
  • Where are Faraz and Sa'ad going?
  • Sa'ad feels embarrassed for his rude behaviour.
  • Did you get up late in the morning?

Writing a Narrative Paragraph

A narrative paragraph retells an event, and it has a beginning, a middle and an ending.

  • the event that happened
  • the characters
  • when and where it took place
  • any message
  • a proper beginning, middle and ending

Writing a Narrative Paragraph

Write a narrative paragraph of your own about an event of your life which you could never forget.

Caring for Differently-Abled People

  • help them without making them feel different
  • speak politely
  • give them ramps, accessible toilets and hearing and visual facilities
  • include them in games and work
  • never make fun of them

lessons.title: The Lesson: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
The Lesson Text

Pakistan is a country with a rich cultural heritage. It is comprised of different cultural groups like Punjabis, Sindhis, Balochis, Pakhtuns, Kashmiris and Gilgit-Baltistanis. These cultural groups reflect a range of amazing traditions, dresses, foods and languages. People from different cultural groups speak a variety of languages. In Punjab, people speak 'Punjabi' and 'Seraiki'. 'Sindhi' and 'Balochi' are common languages of Sindh and Balochistan. In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, people speak 'Pashto', 'Hindko', 'Khowar' and 'Seraiki'. In Gilgit-Baltistan, 'Shina', 'Balti', and 'Burushaski' are regional languages. Kashmiri is spoken in Kashmir. In Pakistan, people wear a wide range of clothes depending on the climate and traditions of the place they belong to. Also local festivals are unique to each cultural group. The culture of the Punjabis is considered one of the oldest and richest cultures in the world. Punjab has always been the land of peace, love and great cultural and artistic values. Punjabi men wear kurta, tahmat and turban. Shalwar kameez or kurta are Punjabi women's traditional dress. A seasonal festival named Jashan-e-Baharan or the Spring Festival is celebrated in Punjab in the mid of February. The culture of Sindh evolved from the Indus Valley Civilisation. Sindhi culture is dominated by great Sufis, mystics and martyrs. The Sindhi cap and ajrak are part of men's dress. Women wear kameez or kurta shalwar. Women also use ajrak as a dupatta or a shawl. People of Sindh celebrate the Sindh festival, Jashan-e-Larkana and many other local festivals. The culture of Balochistan is full of traditions, arts and crafts. Balochistan is also known for its tribes and festivals. Poetry and storytelling are very popular among the Baloch. Balochis wear various styles of kameez, shalwar, turban (kulaah) and headscarfs. 'Phashik' is a traditional Balochi dress. In Balochistan, the Sibbi Festival attracts people from all across the country. Hospitality, hard work and bravery are distinctive features of Pakhtun culture. Pakhtuns follow Pakhtunwali, that is, a traditional lifestyle. Pakhtun culture is famous for its tribal social lifestyle. Pakhtun men usually wear shalwar kameez, waistcoat and shawl with a turban or a pakol hat. Women wear embroidered frocks with pajamas and dupatta. The Polo festival is celebrated every year in Shandur, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Kashmiri culture is reflected in different traditions relating to food, clothing and festivals. Phiran is a prominent traditional dress of Kashmiri men and women. Women wear traditional hand-embroidered clothes. Pirchinasi is celebrated every year in Kashmir. Shina and Balti cultures exist in Gilgit-Baltistan. The people of Baltistan are very cheerful and hospitable. Men usually wear a woolen cap, shalwar kameez and woollen robe with long and short sleeves. Women wear traditional lraghi caps and colourful frocks. The Harvest Festival is celebrated every year in Gilgit-Baltistan. Islamic values and teachings are common factors shared by all cultures of Pakistan. A number of religious and regional festivals are celebrated here. However, let's not forget the minorities and other communities that celebrate their joyful events in the country. The Christian community celebrates Christmas, Easter and other religious festivals in Pakistan. The other minorities like Hindus, Sikhs and Parsis also celebrate their religious days.

National Dress of Pakistan

The national dress of Pakistan is shalwar kameez.

Festivals of Pakistan

Pakistan celebrates many colourful festivals.

Jashan-e-Baharan is celebrated in Punjab, the Sindh festival and Jashan-e-Larkana in Sindh, the Sibbi Festival in Balochistan, the Polo festival in Shandur, Pirchinasi in Kashmir and the Harvest Festival in Gilgit-Baltistan.

These festivals show the rich culture and unity of Pakistan.

Eids in Pakistan

Pakistanis celebrate two Eids in a year — Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Azha.

Religious Festivals

Pakistan celebrates many religious festivals.

Muslims celebrate Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Azha.

The Christian community celebrates Christmas and Easter.

Hindus, Sikhs and Parsis also celebrate their religious days in Pakistan.

Culture of Punjab

Punjab celebrates Jashan-e-Baharan, the Spring Festival, in the mid of February.

Punjabi men wear kurta, tahmat and turban, and women wear shalwar kameez.

Punjab is the land of peace, love and great cultural values.

Students adapt this to his or her own province.

Seasonal Festivals

Jashan-e-Baharan, the Spring Festival, is celebrated in Punjab in the mid of February.

The Harvest Festival is celebrated in Gilgit-Baltistan.

Traditional Dresses

In Sindh, men wear the Sindhi cap and ajrak, and women wear kameez or kurta shalwar and use ajrak as a dupatta or a shawl.

In Kashmir, Phiran is the prominent traditional dress of Kashmiri men and women, and women wear traditional hand-embroidered clothes.

Festivals of Minorities

The Christian community celebrates Christmas and Easter.

Hindus, Sikhs and Parsis also celebrate their religious days.

Key Facts

  • Shinas and Burusho cultures exist in Gilgit-Baltistan.
  • Ajrak is a part of Sindhi culture.
  • Poetry and storytelling are very popular among the Baloch.
  • The spring festival is celebrated in Punjab in the mid of February.
  • The Polo festival is celebrated every year in Shandur.

lessons.notes_html:
Long Vowel Sounds

  • long a — cake, name, brave, game
  • long e — tree, free, sheep, keep
  • long i — kite, bike, kind, find
  • long o — nose, rose, float, boat
  • long u — cute, mule, huge, cube

A vowel's sound is long if it sounds like the vowel's name, for example: a long 'a' in 'sake' and a long 'e' in 'weep'.

Giving Directions

Huma: Assalaamu Alaikum, Irum! How are you?

Irum: Wa Alaikum Assalaam, I am good. Where are you coming from?

Huma: I am coming from a flower exhibition. It was really very beautiful and colourful.

Irum: Wow! That's really great. I also wanted to go there. Can you please tell me the way to the flower exhibition?

Huma: Yes, sure. First, go right. You will find a masjid at the corner. Then turn left and then turn second right. After a few steps, you will find the flower exhibition being held in a garden.

Irum: Thank you for your guidance.

Huma: You are welcome.

Speaking Practice

Conduct a role-play activity and tell your friend the way to your house using the expressions of directions.

mcqs.why: Tree has the long e sound, like free, sheep and keep; a vowel's sound is long if it sounds like the vowel's name.

mcqs.why: The directions are: go right, find the masjid at the corner, turn left, and then turn second right.

lessons.notes_html:
Colours of Pakistan

We are Pakistanis and we love our country. Colour the part of the political map of Pakistan which you belong to, and conduct a group discussion about the cultural aspects — food, language, dresses, festivals and other aspects — of different areas of Pakistan and share it with the class.

Reading a Map

  • Road
  • Masjid
  • Hospital
  • Home
  • Zigzag road
  • Railway track
  • Park
  • Water tank
  • Bridge

Use the key symbols of the city map to locate the places on the map.

Keywords, verbs and tenses used in a question can help us a lot to identify the question type.

Factual questions help us to find the answers in the form of facts directly from the text.

Analytical Reading

Read more information about the different areas of Pakistan from the internet and note down some important points about their local festivals in your notebook.

Vocabulary

  • culture — a way of life, or customs and beliefs of people
  • tradition — a belief, custom or way of living
  • distinctive — special and unique
  • cheerful — happy
  • dominate — effective

These meanings are as printed in the book.

Compound Words

  • fingerprint — finger + print
  • toothpaste — tooth + paste

Compound Words

  • strawberries — straw + berries
  • notebook — note + book
  • sunflowers — sun + flowers
  • password — pass + word
  • cupcakes — cup + cakes
  • shopkeeper — shop + keeper

Learning to Spell

The correct spellings are artistic, religious, sacrifice, festival and hospitality.

Pronouns

  • This is my favourite painting. It is very beautiful.
  • Uzma and Asma are neighbours. They study together.
  • Can I borrow your Kashmiri dress?
  • Umar is very busy today. He is preparing for the competition.

'Be', 'Do' and 'Have' with Pronouns

  • I — I am a student. (main) I am reading a story. (helping) I have a rabbit. (main) I have memorised the lesson. (helping)
  • We — We had a house. (main) We had bought a house. (helping) We did our homework. (main) We did not go there. (helping)
  • You — You are late. (main) You are going to the mall. (helping) You had a backache. (main) You had eaten a sandwich. (helping)
  • He/She — He/she is cute. (main) He/she was writing a story. (helping) He/she has two siblings. (main) He/she has gone shopping. (helping)
  • It — It is a small bunny. (main) It was jumping. (helping) It has beautiful hair. (main) It has drunk water. (helping)
  • They — They have a bicycle. (main) They have played football. (helping) They had no bicycle. (main) They do not play cricket. (helping)

The verbs be, do and have and their different forms are used as main and helping verbs.

When they are used as helping verbs with the main verb, they help the action of the sentence.

When they are used alone, they are main verbs.

Punctuation

  • Balochistan is also known for its tribes and festivals.
  • Where is Shandur located?
  • Wow! You look pretty in Sindhi dress!
  • When is Eid-ul-Azha celebrated?
  • The Horse and Cattle Show is a local festival.

Festival Words

  • Spring Festival — kites, flowers
  • Horse and Cattle Show — horse, camel, cow

Food is needed at both festivals.

Writing a Dialogue

A: Did you ever attend the Spring Festival?

B: Yes, we went there last year.

A: What did you enjoy most?

B: The kites, flowers and colourful dresses.

A: Have you attended the Horse and Cattle Show?

B: Yes, I saw horses, camels and cows there.

A: Festivals show the colours of Pakistan.

B: Yes, every province has its own beautiful festivals.

Creative Writing

Share your experience of a cultural festival you attended in a short paragraph.

  • the name of the festival
  • where and when it was held
  • what you saw — dresses, food, dances
  • what you enjoyed most

lessons.title: The Lesson: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Good Manners

Good manners are important because they show respect for others and make life pleasant for everyone.

Good manners include respect for elders, dressing neatly, caring for one another, healthy eating habits and washing hands.

The Lesson Text

Last week, Miss Hina told us to make a poster about good study habits. My brother and I started making the poster. We found out that good study habits could help us to become better students. We can improve our reading and writing skills. All good students follow these habits. We should also adopt these habits. When the poster was completed, we displayed it in our classroom. Miss Hina asked us to share the importance of good study habits with our classmates.

Good study habits:

  • Set your goals for study.
  • Make a timetable for studying.
  • Make notes in your notebooks.
  • Work on the topic you find the most difficult first.
  • Revise classwork at the weekend.
  • Don't spend too much time watching television.
  • Get information from books, your teachers and parents.

I tried to adopt all these study habits. Within a few days, I got good results. In my final term, I got first position in my class. I was really excited. My parents arranged a party for my friends and cousins to celebrate my success. So, I wrote an invitation to one of my cousins.

March 31, 2022. Dear Asif, How are you? I got first position in my final exams and want to celebrate this success with my friends and family. I am arranging a party on this Friday evening at my house. You are invited to join us. It'll be great fun. Hope to see you on Friday. Your cousin, Maheen.

The Poster

The poster was displayed in our classroom.

Good Study Habits

Good habits of my own: I revise my classwork every day. I make notes in my notebook while studying.

We should follow good study habits because they help us to become better students, improve our reading and writing skills, and get good results in exams.

Reading Comprehension

Miss Hina asked the students to make a poster about good study habits.

Two good study habits mentioned in the story are: set your goals for study, and make a timetable for studying.

Her parents arranged a party to celebrate her success, because she got first position in her final term.

Alphabetical Order

In alphabetical order according to the second letter: bake (a), bee (e), bite (i), blue (l), bring (r), butter (u).

Alphabetical order by first letter, for example: cat, centre, change, class, habit, pool.

Note-taking: 'First Prize'

New words: sweating, success, wipe, glad.

Important points: Danish worked hard to gain good marks. His parents also helped him. He stood first in his exams. He wrote a letter to them.

Note-taking is a technique to gather information about a topic. It is very useful.

Key Facts

  • Miss Hina asked students to make a poster.
  • The poster was displayed in the classroom.
  • Good study habits can help us become better students.
  • We should make a timetable for studying.

Analytical Reading

Make a list of ten eating habits and write them down in your notebook.

Vocabulary

  • planner — timetable
  • celebrate — to do something special to show happiness
  • display — show
  • invite — to request someone to attend an event

Adjectives

Pairs of adjectives that may have a similar meaning but different strength: fresh / new; dutiful / obedient; silent / quiet; amazing / great.

Adjectives are words which describe nouns in phrases or sentences.

Spelling

improve, display, poster, celebrate, arrange.

Pronouns

  • I (subject) — me (object): Allah (SWT) loves me. I love Allah (SWT).
  • We (subject) — us (object): We study together. Come study with us.
  • You (subject) — you (object): Ali likes you. You like Ali.
  • He (subject) — him (object): He is my classmate. I play with him.
  • She (subject) — her (object): She is my best friend. I love her.
  • It (subject) — it (object): It is a colourful dress. Maha likes it.
  • They (subject) — them (object): They go to the park. Ali also goes with them.

Possessive Pronouns

  • The bag is yours. You forgot to take it with you.
  • The cycle belongs to Amir. It is his.
  • These shops are ours. We work here.
  • That old car was mine. I have sold it.
  • They are in the apple orchard. That orchard is theirs.
  • It is his book, not hers.

Possessive pronouns are the words that show possession in sentences or phrases.

Can, Cannot, May and May Not

Sa'ad can work in a bank but he cannot teach in a school. He can ride a bike but he cannot drive a car.

May I go to drink water? May I use your pencil? You may not leave the classroom now.

Can and cannot are used to show some ability or inability in sentences. May and may not are used to ask or deny permission in sentences.

Adverbs

  • My mother speaks politely.
  • The birthday party was decorated beautifully.
  • She wrote a story neatly.
  • She cleans the room hurriedly.
  • The old woman walked slowly.

Adverbs are words which add some meaning to the verbs, adjectives and adverbs.

Punctuation

The last time I went to Murree, it rained all day. I forgot my umbrella, so I got soaked. Have you ever done that? It was really a very silly thing to do. Next time I'll be careful.

The punctuation in these sentences has been reconstructed from the unpunctuated text.

Invitations and Notes

Dear Asif, You are invited to my birthday party on Friday evening at my house. It'll be great fun. Hope to see you. Your friend, Maheen.

Short notes are informal letters. An invitation shows purpose, date and time, venue, name of addressee and sender.

Dear Maheen, Thank you for your invitation. I will come to your birthday party on Friday evening. I am really excited. Your friend, Asif.

Classroom Rules

Make a chart of your own and write some classroom rules on it. Model rules:

  • Raise your hand before speaking.
  • Respect your teachers and classmates.
  • Keep the classroom clean.
  • Do your homework on time.

lessons.notes_html:
Helping at Home

I keep my room tidy. I help my mother at home by cleaning my room, washing the dishes and keeping my things in their places.

The pictures show ways to express feelings about good manners.

The Poem

Whole Duty of Children, by Robert Louis Stevenson:

A child should always say what's true
And speak when he is spoken to,
And behave mannerly at table;
At least as far as he is able.

Washing Hands

We should always wash our hands with soap before and after a meal to remove germs and dirt and to stay healthy.

Table Manners

  • Sit properly at the table.
  • Wash your hands before eating.
  • Eat quietly with your mouth closed.
  • Do not talk with food in your mouth.
  • Do not waste food.
  • Say thanks after the meal.

Main Idea of the Poem

The main idea of the poem is that a child should always be truthful, polite and well-mannered — say what is true, speak when spoken to, and behave mannerly at table as far as he is able.

Table Manners

A child should behave mannerly at table.

  • Sit properly.
  • Wash hands with soap before eating.
  • Eat quietly.
  • Do not talk with food in your mouth.
  • Do not waste food.
  • Thank after the meal.

Table of Contents

The title of the book is English. The title of unit 3 is The Journey of Chocolate. The title of the unit that starts on page 13 is Beauty of Nature.

  • Unit 1 — Great Caliphs of Islam
  • Unit 2 — Beauty of Nature, page 13
  • Unit 3 — The Journey of Chocolate, page 22

The table of contents helps us to find different chapters in a book.

Key Facts

  • The poet Robert Louis Stevenson wrote the poem 'Whole Duty of Children'.
  • In the poem, the poet is talking about manners.
  • A child should always say what is true.
  • A child should behave mannerly at the table.

Analytical Reading

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
Three Sounds of -ed

  • /t/ — helped, thanked, pushed
  • /d/ — rubbed, loved, closed
  • /id/ — wanted, motivated, started

If the -ed ending follows the letters p, k, sh, ch, s, f, th, then the ending sound will be 't'.

If the -ed ending follows the letters b, g, i, j, l, m, n, o, u, v, z, then the ending sound will be 'd'.

If the -ed ending follows the letters 't' or 'd', then the ending sound will be 'id'.

More examples: /d/: loved, tired, behaved. /id/: visited, painted, decided. /t/: watched, dropped, asked.

Dialogue: Personal Hygiene

Sidra: Good morning, Mama.

Mother: Good morning, dear Sidra.

Sidra: Mama, shall I come and help you prepare breakfast for me?

Mother: Yes, sure. First tell me, have you brushed your teeth and taken a shower?

Sidra: Yes, I have brushed my teeth, but haven't taken a shower yet.

Mother: Go and take a shower first, then I will serve you breakfast. We should always take care of our personal hygiene.

Sidra: Okay sure, Mama.

Group Discussion

Take part in a group discussion and share some good manners which you adopt in your daily lives.

mcqs.why: Helped ends with the /t/ sound, like thanked and pushed; -ed sounds /t/ after p, k, sh, ch, s, f and th.

mcqs.why: Loved ends with the /d/ sound, like rubbed and closed; -ed sounds /d/ after b, g, l, m, n, v, z and vowel sounds.

mcqs.why: Wanted ends with /id/ because the verb ends in 't'; -ed sounds /id/ after t or d, as in motivated, started, visited and decided.

mcqs.why: If the -ed ending follows the letters 't' or 'd', the ending sound will be 'id', as in wanted and decided.

mcqs.why: Watched is listed among the /t/ examples with dropped and asked, because 'watch' ends with the ch sound.

options: Have you brushed your teeth and taken a shower?
mcqs.why: Mother asks, 'Have you brushed your teeth and taken a shower?' and sends Sidra to take a shower first, teaching personal hygiene.

mcqs.why: Sidra says, 'Yes, I have brushed my teeth, but haven't taken a shower yet,' so she goes to take a shower first.

options: Good manners they adopt in their daily lives
mcqs.why: Students take part in a group discussion and share some good manners which they adopt in their daily lives.

mcqs.why: Visited and painted are given as /id/ examples because both verbs end in the letter t.

mcqs.why: Behaved and tired are listed among the /d/ examples with loved, because the -ed follows voiced sounds.

lessons.title: Language Focus and Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • behave — act
  • mannerly — in a way that shows good manners
  • at least — not less than
  • able — to have the skill to do something

Similes

The field is as green as grass. The rose is red as blood. The sky shines as blue as heaven. The star shines like a diamond in the sky.

A simile is a word or phrase used to compare two things by using the words 'like' or 'as', for example: 'as brave as a lion', 'like a diamond'.

An emerald is as green as grass; a ruby is red as blood; a sapphire shines as blue as heaven; a flint lies in the mud.

Twinkle, twinkle little star, how I wonder what you are, up above the world so high, like a diamond in the sky.

Spelling

behave, table, spoken, child, true.

Possessive Pronouns

  • I had bought my new phone.
  • We have sold our old house.
  • Ali is working on his computer.
  • Could you please give me your camera?
  • She has lost her handbag.
  • The parrot is eating its food.

A possessive pronoun shows ownership. My, our, your, his, her, etc. are possessive pronouns.

Should and Should Not

We should not speak rudely to our elders. You should go to school on time. She should not eat too many chocolates. He should study hard to get first position. We should follow good manners.

Should is used to make recommendations, to give advice or opinion, and to talk about an obligation. Should not is used in negative sentences.

Examples: We should drink at least eight glasses of water every day. You should listen to your teacher carefully. Abeera should complete her homework on time. You should take some rest after a long trip. Children should not watch a lot of television. We should not make fun of others.

We should respect our elders. You should wash your hands before meals. She should speak the truth. He should not tell lies. We should not waste food. They should arrive on time.

Joining Words

A child should speak and behave mannerly at the table. Do you want to eat pancakes or eggs for breakfast? Umar wanted to drive to the mall, but his car wouldn't start. My mother bought fruit and vegetables from the market. Mina reads storybooks, but she doesn't like to read the newspaper. Do you like to play football or basketball?

Joining words are used to join words or sentences. Some joining words are 'and', 'or', 'but', etc.

Adverbs of Manner

The adverbs are: easily, warmly, regularly, carefully, luckily.

Adverbs of manner tell us the manner or way in which something happens. Examples: Sara washes her hands slowly. Ahmad plays the piano beautifully. They walked in the park quickly. Speak to your elders politely.

Punctuation

We should wash our hands with soap before and after every meal. Wow! What an interesting story! My uncle is a good-looking man. Father bought some eggs, onions, tomatoes and potatoes.

Central Idea of the Poem

Central idea: A child should always speak the truth, speak when spoken to, and behave mannerly at table as far as he is able — in short, a child should always practise good manners.

The central idea of a poem discusses the main thought of the whole poem. It is also called the main idea.

Rhyming Words and a Poem

Rhyming pairs: teeth/neat, brush/rush, clean/gleam, day/play.

Brush your teeth both night and day,
Keep them clean in every way.
Do not rush, take time to brush,
Then your smile will gleam and play.

Writing a Poem

Please do not make a fuss,
Be kind to all of us.
Turn to what you find,
And learn to be kind.

Vocabulary

Modal Verbs

I can ride a bike. May I use your pencil? We should respect our elders. You must wash your hands before meals. I will come to your party.

The modal verbs practised in Units 8-9 are can/cannot, may/may not and should/should not.

Adverbs

The adverbs are: slowly, almost, generously, hungrily, happily.

Punctuation

Yasir went to visit a nearby market with his uncle. He was very happy to see different kinds of things. He saw fresh fruit and vegetables. The fruit and vegetables were so colourful. He asked his uncle where the pet shop was. Then they went to the pet shop. 'Wow! What a beautiful cat this is!' he said to his uncle.

Possessive Pronouns

Our neighbour asked my family and me to water their plants while they were on vacation. Monday will be my day to water. My brother offered to take his turn on Tuesday and Wednesday. My mother will take her turn on Thursday and Friday. So my father only has to water on the weekend.

The pronouns in these sentences have been fitted from the sentence context.

Writing a Dialogue

A: How shall we celebrate the Spring Festival in our school?

A: Good idea! We can also wear colourful dresses.

B: Yes, and we can sing songs and share sweets.

lessons.title: The Lesson: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
Staying Safe from Strangers

I would not talk to strangers or accept anything from them. I would ignore them and go to a safe place, and tell my parents.

Brother: Have you seen them before? Sister: No, they seem to be strangers. Brother: Watch out, they are coming towards us. Sister: Yes, we should not talk to strangers, or accept anything from them. Brother: Oh, yes! Let's ignore them.

The Lesson Text

Sara was holding a doll when Sara and her brother Ahsan entered their home.

Sara: Hello, Mama. Look, what I have got!

Mother: Who gave you this doll?

Sara: There was a man in the street.

Mother: Come here, Sara and Ahsan, and sit by my side.

Sara and her brother sat with their mother on the sofa.

Mother: You are good kids. Listen to me carefully.

Sara: Okay, Mama!

Mother: You should not get friendly with people whom you don't know. Never take anything from them without telling me or your Baba.

Sara: Why, Mama? Is it wrong?

Mother: Yes, it is not good to accept gifts from strangers.

Sara: Sorry, Mama. I won't do it again.

Ahsan: Mama, why is it wrong to be friendly with strangers?

Mother: Because it might be dangerous for you.

Ahsan: Okay, Mama!

Sara: If someone comes close to me, what should I do?

Mother: If a stranger ever comes close to you and offers a ride, a toy or any candy or chocolate, you should step away and say 'No!' to him. Leave that place quickly. Remember, your Baba and I trust you a lot. So, share your daily routine and secrets with us instead of anyone else.

Sara: Which secrets, Mama?

Mother: If you leave class/school without informing your teacher, you should share it with me. If someone makes you feel uncomfortable or if you feel like something is just not right, you need to walk away at once and also share the incident with me. Promise me.

Ahsan: Promise, Mama!

Sara: I promise, I will share all my activities with you.

Mother: Good girl. I love both of you.

Safety from Strangers

I will not allow a stranger to come closer to me.

Safety from Strangers

If a stranger offers me a toy, I would step away and say 'No!' to him, leave that place quickly, and tell my parents.

Safety from Strangers

It is not right to get anything from a stranger. It is not good to accept gifts from strangers.

Staying Safe from Strangers

We should not take things from strangers because it might be dangerous for us.

Staying Safe from Strangers

If any stranger comes to me, I will step away, say 'No!', leave that place quickly, and tell my parents or teacher.

Sara's Doll

A man in the street, a stranger, gave a doll to Sara.

Being Friendly with Strangers

It is wrong to be friendly with strangers because it might be dangerous for you.

Taking Things from Strangers

We should not take things from strangers. We should never accept gifts, rides, toys, candy or chocolate from strangers without telling our parents.

Elements of a Story

  • Characters — people or animals who take part in the action of a story.
  • Setting — the place and time where the story events take place.
  • Beginning — it provides answers to who, when and where questions. In the beginning of a story, the writer describes the characters and setting.
  • Middle — it contains all the actions of a story.
  • Conflict — every story has a problem that makes the characters work and get it solved.
  • Ending — it is the solution to the conflict.

The September Calendar

In September there are 5 Fridays: 3, 10, 17, 24 and 31.

There are 23 school days in September, counted as Monday to Friday weekdays.

The calendar as printed runs to 31 days and starts on Wednesday, though September normally has 30 days.

Key Sentences from the Lesson

  • We should not accept gifts from strangers.
  • If any stranger comes to us, we should say 'No!' to him/her.
  • If you feel uncomfortable with any person, you should walk away at once.
  • We should share our secrets with our parents.
  • If any stranger tries to be friendly with us, it might cause harm to us.

Weak Forms

  • Day and night.
  • The chair is made of wood.
  • The food is good but the service is bad.
  • Are you ready or not?
  • Black and white.

Weak forms are syllable sounds that become unstressed in speech. For example: of, and, or, but.

Learning to Speak

Teacher: Haris, come to the front and read the lesson. Jawad: Sir, can I come first? Teacher: No, you have to wait for your turn. Jawad: Okay, sir.

Speaking Activity: Sharing

Create and practise a dialogue session between two friends on sharing, taking turns and using polite expressions to seek attention.

lessons.title: Language Focus and Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Writing Your Own Story

Think and outline a story of your own, keeping the story elements in view, and share your story with your teacher and classmates.

Analytical Reading

Read the story 'Aladdin and the Magic Lamp' and share your opinion, whether you like or dislike the story, with your classmates.

Vocabulary

  • carefully — with a lot of attention
  • stranger — a person that you do not know
  • friendly — showing that somebody is kind
  • harmful — dangerous
  • uncomfortable — uneasy

Parts of Speech

  • Noun — Sara, mother, home
  • Verbs — permit, promise, accept
  • Adjectives — nice, harsh, dangerous
  • Pronouns — you, they, it

Learning to Spell

The completed words are: chocolate, candies, stranger, promise, secret.

Pronoun-Antecedent Agreement

Once, Sara's mother was working in the kitchen. Sara went to the kitchen to help her mother. She decided to wash the dishes. She turned on the water tap and started soaping the dishes. Her mother saw her and she advised Sara to turn off the tap while she was soaping the dishes. She told Sara that we should not waste water. Sara and her mother washed the dishes. After that, they cooked food and cleaned the kitchen. In the evening, they enjoyed their meal.

Pronoun-antecedent agreement means pronouns must agree with their antecedents in gender and number. If the antecedent is of feminine gender, the pronoun must be of the same gender. If an antecedent is singular, the pronoun must represent a single person, place or thing.

Paragraph Writing

Write a paragraph on 'Respect for Family Members', taking care of pronoun-antecedent agreement.

Regular Verbs

  • start → started → started
  • play → played → played
  • touch → touched → touched
  • decide → decided → decided

Regular verbs form their past and past participle forms by adding -d or -ed to them.

Regular Verbs

  • ask → asked → asked
  • need → needed → needed
  • demand → demanded → demanded
  • accept → accepted → accepted

Present, Past and Future Tenses

  • Present — Sara plays with a doll. Mother explains stranger's danger to Sara.
  • Past — Sara played with a doll. Mother explained stranger's danger to Sara.
  • Future — Sara will play with a doll. Mother will explain stranger's danger to Sara.

The present tense shows actions which happen in the present. The past tense shows actions that happened in the past. The future tense shows actions that will happen in the future.

Present, Past and Future Tenses

  • Ali writes a letter to his uncle — Present (simple present).
  • They will water the plants — Future.
  • I will go to Gilgit next month — Future.

Adverbs of Time

  • He saw a stranger outside his house yesterday.
  • I will call you later.
  • I'm going to Lahore tomorrow.
  • We are doing our homework now.

Adverbs of time tell us when something happens. They express a point in time. For example: tonight, yesterday, tomorrow, daily, weekly.

Abbreviations

  • November → Nov.
  • minute → min.
  • Limited → Ltd.

An abbreviation is a shortened form of a word.

Abbreviations

  • Aug. → August
  • St. → Street
  • Dr. → Doctor
  • Dept. → Department

Guided Writing

Think of a story of your own and fill in a story web with the character, setting, the beginning, conflict, the middle and solution, then write a story of your own using that information in your notebook, revising your written work for correct spelling and punctuation.

Rules for Staying Safe

  • Do not talk to strangers.
  • Do not accept gifts, rides, toys, candy or chocolate from strangers.
  • If a stranger comes close, step away and say 'No!'.
  • Leave that place quickly.
  • Share your daily routine and secrets with your parents only.
  • Do not leave class or school without informing your teacher.
  • If someone makes you feel uncomfortable, walk away at once and tell your parents.
