chapters.title: Unit 11: The Fox And The Stork

lessons.title: The Lesson: Reading and Comprehension
lessons.notes_html:
True Friends

In the pictures, a boy is helping his friend up, and a mouse is helping a lion — true friends help one another. Friends also share things, play together, help in studies and comfort each other. I can be a good friend by being kind, honest, helpful and by never making fun of anyone.

The pictures show what true friends do for one another.

The Lesson Text

Once there were a fox and a stork living in a jungle. The fox was very clever. He always teased others. One day, he decided to play a trick on the stork. He went to his home and invited him to a dinner. The stork went to his place for the meal. The fox prepared a tasty soup and served it in flat plates cunningly. The stork was unable to sip as his beak was so long. It was difficult for him to eat from the flat dish. The hungry stork got angry but he did not show his anger and quickly went home. The stork had understood the scheme of the fox. He decided to teach the fox a lesson. He invited him to dinner the next evening. The fox arrived happily at his place. The stork served the meal in a jar with a narrow neck. The stork easily ate all his food with his long beak, but the fox could not. He could not put her mouth into the jar.

The stork said to the fox calmly, 'Do not ridicule or degrade anyone for any reason. Allah (SWT) has made us all equal.' The fox was ashamed. He said sorry to the stork. They became friends again.

The Stork's Answer

The stork will teach the fox a lesson — he invites the fox to dinner and serves the meal in a jar with a narrow neck.

The Moral of the Story

We should not ridicule or degrade anyone for any reason. Allah (SWT) has made us all equal. We should treat our friends with kindness and respect.

The Stork

I liked the stork the most because he was calm, wise and forgiving — he taught the fox a lesson without anger and became friends with him again.

The Fox's Trick

The fox decided to play a trick on the stork.

How the Meal Was Served

The fox prepared a tasty soup and served it in flat plates, cunningly.

Treating Friends

We should treat our friends with kindness, respect and equality. We should never ridicule or degrade anyone, share with them, help them, and forgive them when they say sorry.

Elements of a Fable

  • Characters — the fox and the stork
  • Setting — a jungle
  • Plot — the fox tricks the stork with soup in flat plates; the stork teaches the fox a lesson with food in a narrow-necked jar
  • Conflict — the fox ridiculed the stork
  • Resolution — the fox said sorry and they became friends again

Characters are the persons or animals in a story. Setting is the time and place where the story happens. Plot is the events that make up a story. Conflict is a problem between characters. Resolution is the point when the problem between characters is solved.

Key Facts

  • The stork could not eat the meal.
  • The fox was very clever.
  • The fox served the meal in flat plates.
  • The fox and stork became friends.

options: He invited the fox to dinner and served the meal in a jar with a narrow neck
He stopped talking to the fox

options: Never come to my home again
Do not ridicule or degrade anyone for any reason; Allah (SWT) has made us all equal
mcqs.why: The stork said calmly, 'Do not ridicule or degrade anyone for any reason. Allah (SWT) has made us all equal.' This is the moral of the story.

mcqs.q: What did the fox do at the end?
options: He was ashamed, said sorry, and they became friends again
mcqs.why: The fox was ashamed; he said sorry to the stork, and they became friends again.

mcqs.why: The story begins: 'Once there were a fox and a stork living in a jungle.' The setting of the fable is a jungle.

options: Very clever, and he always teased others
mcqs.why: The fox was very clever and he always teased others; the stork was calm, wise and forgiving.

mcqs.q: In the fable, what is the 'resolution'?
options: The fox said sorry and they became friends again
mcqs.why: Resolution is the point when the problem is solved: the fox said sorry and they became friends again.

mcqs.q: How should we treat our friends, according to the lesson?
options: With kindness, respect and equality, and never ridicule anyone
mcqs.why: We should treat our friends with kindness, respect and equality, share with them, help them, and forgive them when they say sorry.

mcqs.q: Why did the narrator like the stork the most?
options: He was calm, wise and forgiving, and taught the fox a lesson without anger
mcqs.why: The stork was liked most because he was calm, wise and forgiving — he taught the fox a lesson without anger and became friends with him again.

lessons.title: Sounds and Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
Intonation Patterns

  • Do they follow traffic signs? — rising (yes-no question)
  • Always walk on the footpath. — falling (command)
  • Why are you driving fast? — falling (wh-question)
  • Hurrah! I came first. — falling (exclamation)

Intonation tells us how the voice rises and falls in a speech.

Rising intonation means our voice rises at the end of a statement, for example: We should follow traffic rules; and in yes-no questions, for example: Do you obey traffic rules?

Falling intonation means our voice falls on the final stressed syllable of a phrase or a group of words, for example: Accidents can happen anywhere; in wh-questions, for example: What is your name; in commands, for example: Do not run on roads; in exclamations, for example: That's great!

Learning to Speak

Stork: Hello, how are you, friends (fox and monkey)? Fox: I am fine. Thank you. Monkey: I am also fine. Stork: Where are you both going? Monkey: We are going to drink water from the new pond. It is really beautiful. Fox: Yes, it is. Stork: Wow, I also want to go there but now I am in a hurry. By the way where is it? Fox: It is to the left of the big oak tree. Stork: Thank you, both of you. Monkey: You are welcome.

Speaking Activity: Qualities of a Good Friend

Make a group of three students and discuss qualities of a good friend, agreeing and disagreeing by using polite words.

mcqs.why: Wh-questions take falling intonation: 'Why are you driving fast?' and 'What is your name?'

options: Falling, because it is an exclamation
Rising, because it is a question
mcqs.why: Exclamations have falling intonation: 'Hurrah! I came first.' and 'That's great!'

options: To a pond to drink water

lessons.title: Language Focus and Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Analytical Reading

Read any fable and find out its moral, and write the moral in your notebook.

Vocabulary

  • clever — sharp; quick at learning
  • teased — made fun of
  • beak — curved outer part of a bird's mouth
  • degrade — to make people feel that they have no value
  • served — offer something to eat

Parts of Speech

  • Verb — invited, served
  • Noun — fox, stork
  • Adjective — clever, tasty
  • Pronoun — he, him
  • Adverb — happily, calmly
  • Preposition — in, to
  • Conjunction — and, but

In English, we have different parts of speech: noun, pronoun, verb, etc. They are also called word classes.

Alphabetical Order

  • beak (beak) /bi:k/ noun — the hard pointed or curved outer part of a bird's mouth
  • beam (beam) /bi:m/ noun — a line of light, electric waves or particles
  • bean (bean) /bi:n/ noun — a seed, or pod containing seeds

Words are arranged in alphabetical order. A dictionary helps to find the meanings of words. It has all words arranged in alphabetical order.

Alphabetical Order

The words in alphabetical order are: ashamed, cunning, degrade, favourite, greediness, jar, meal, narrow, place, pluck.

Learning to Spell

The completed words are: cunning, stork, stranger, friend, food.

Subject, Object and Possessive Pronouns

  • Subject pronouns — I am ten years old. You look tired today. Rehan is angry, and he wants Salman to apologise. This table is old. It needs repairing. We are not coming. They do not like these cakes.
  • Object pronouns — Give this book to me. Ali wants to talk to you. Junaid is hurt because Hamza hit him. Rida received a letter from her last week. Maryam cannot find it. Don't be angry with us.
  • Possessive pronouns — This bag is mine. This bag is yours. That dress looks like his. These shoes are not hers. That house is ours. This isn't our car. It's theirs.

Subject pronouns are used as the subject of the verb. Object pronouns are used as the object of the verb. Possessive pronouns show possession or ownership.

Subject, Object and Possessive Pronouns

  • Subject — I am a student. They play cricket.
  • Object — Give the book to me. Ali helped him.
  • Possessive — This pen is mine. That house is ours.

Tenses

The Simple Present Tense — The fox eats grapes. The fox does not eat grapes. Does the fox eat grapes? The simple present tense is used for actions that take place in the present. We use the present form of the verb to make the simple present tense.

The Simple Continuous Tense — Villagers are eating. Villagers are not eating. Are villagers eating? The present continuous tense is used to express an ongoing action at the time of speaking.

The Simple Past Tense — The stork went to the fox's place. The stork did not go to the fox's place. Did the stork go to the fox's place? The simple past tense is used for actions that took place in the past. We add 'd' or 'ed' to the present form to convert it to the past form.

Tenses

  • Simple present — I read a book. She drinks milk.
  • Present continuous — I am reading a book. They are playing cricket.
  • Simple past — I read a book yesterday. She drank milk in the morning.

Joining Words

  • I have two goldfish and a cat.
  • Rida speaks French but she had never been to France.
  • Would you prefer coffee or tea?
  • I got wet because I didn't take an umbrella.
  • He was very hungry so he ate all the cake.

Some words are used to connect words, phrases, and sentences. These words are called joining words.

Question Words

  • Why are you late today?
  • Where do you live?
  • What is behind the door?
  • Which is your bag?

Question words are used to ask questions.

Question Words

Why are you happy today? Where is your school?

The Apostrophe

  • do not → don't
  • could not → couldn't
  • they are → they're
  • I am → I'm

We use the apostrophe (') to mark the omitted letters in contractions. When we combine two words, we omit some letters.

Learning to Write

Think of a story of your own and fill in a mind map to organise your ideas — character, setting, story, plot, conflict, resolution — then write your own story using the ideas organised in the mind map.

Creative Writing

Write a story about how two friends revive their friendship after a quarrel: two friends quarrel over a game; both feel sad; one says sorry; they forgive each other and play together again. Moral: a true friend forgives.

lessons.notes_html:
Classroom Rules

The most important classroom rule is to listen, because we learn when we listen. Every class needs to follow rules so that everyone can learn in peace. Rules are also needed at other places — at home, on the road and in the park — because rules keep us safe and make life fair for everyone. The Classroom Rules chart says: Raise your hand. Listen. Be friendly. Help clean up.

The Lesson Text

Ahsan came home and greeted his father: “Good afternoon, Dad! I have something important to show you.” His father replied, “Good afternoon, my son! I would love to see what you have.” Ahsan took out a brochure from his bag and showed it to his father. He said his teacher had given him the brochure on traffic rules and that it had very interesting information about road safety. His father read the brochure and said everyone should follow traffic rules because these rules make us safe while travelling.

When travelling in cars:

  • Fasten your seatbelt.
  • Always sit quietly in the back seat.
  • Always get out on the kerb side of the car.

When walking to and from school:

  • Avoid crossing between parked cars.
  • Follow traffic signals.
  • Obey traffic police.
  • Cross only at zebra crossing.
  • Always walk and never run.
  • Look to your left and right before crossing the road.
  • Watch for turning vehicles.

When cycling to school:

  • Wear a helmet.
  • Use zebra crossing while crossing the road.
  • Obey the traffic rules.

Ahsan said his father was right, but everyone does not follow the rules, and there is always a traffic jam in front of his school. His father asked if there was no traffic police there. Ahsan said he did not think so and had never seen anyone there. His father said that was not good and that they should inform the traffic police about this issue. As a good citizen, it is our moral duty to help the police by informing them about traffic issues. His father offered to help him write a letter. Here is the letter that Ahsan wrote to the head of traffic police.

Ahsan, House No. 123, Sector A, Islamabad. (Writer's address.)

Inspector General, Traffic Police Headquarters, Islamabad. (Receiver's address.)

22 February 2018. (Date.)

Respected Sir, (Salutation.)

I am writing this letter to inform you about the traffic jam issue in front of The Little Primary School. Nobody follows the traffic rules because there is no traffic police on this road. I often get late for school due to this traffic jam. I also observe many people violating safety rules on the road. They risk their lives and create problems for others as well. I request you to solve this issue to help the citizens of this area.

Yours sincerely, (Signature.)

Traffic Lights

Red means stop. Yellow means get ready (wait). Green means go.

Rules for Cyclists

Cyclists should also follow traffic rules — wear a helmet, use zebra crossing while crossing the road, and obey the traffic rules.

How Traffic Rules Help Us

Traffic rules make us safe while travelling. They prevent accidents and traffic jams.

A Traffic Jam Experience

A traffic jam can be experienced in front of a school. One solution is to tell a parent about it and write a letter to the traffic police, like Ahsan did.

The Brochure

The brochure was about traffic rules and road safety.

Ahsan's Letter

Ahsan wrote the letter to the Inspector General, Traffic Police Headquarters, Islamabad, to inform him about the traffic jam issue in front of The Little Primary School and to request him to solve it.

Traffic in Our City

In a city there can be a lot of traffic in the morning and evening, and there can be traffic jams near schools and markets. People should follow traffic rules, use zebra crossings and obey the traffic police. An interpretive question has more than one answer that can be explained with the help of examples from the text.

Prepositions

The family is standing in front of the camp. Clouds are above the mountains. Ali is sitting between his mother and father. The trees are behind the tent. The boys are standing next to the camp. These sentences show the use of prepositions in a camping picture.

Picture Description

In a living room picture, the position words in, on, between, under, in front of, behind, right and left are used to describe the picture. The red sofa is on the left side of the room. The table is in front of the sofa. The lamp is behind the sofa. The television is on the right side of the room. The books are on the table. The window is behind the chairs.

Picture Description

First, the girl is watering a small plant in a pot near the window. Then, the plant has grown big with white flowers.

Key Facts

  • Ahsan took out a brochure from his bag.
  • The brochure was about traffic rules.
  • The traffic rules make us safe while travelling.
  • Ahsan wrote a letter to the head of the traffic police.

Weak Forms

We need some sugar and tea leaves. The food is tasty but the quantity is less. Is this for us or for them? That is part of the problem. Weak forms are syllable sounds that become unstressed in speech. Examples are 'of', 'and', 'or' and 'but'.

Weak Forms

I want bread and butter. This book is made of paper. Do you want milk or juice? The pen is small but useful. These sentences use the weak forms 'and', 'of', 'or' and 'but'.

Dialogues: Expressing Needs and Feelings

Usman: Wa Alaikum Assalaam. Actually, my grandfather is not feeling well. I am going to get medicine for him.

Sara: Why?

lessons.title: Language Focus and Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • citizen — a person living permanently in a particular society or country
  • headquarters — main offices
  • traffic police — an official who controls traffic
  • walker — a person who walks, especially for exercise or enjoyment

Spellings

travelling, brochure, strange, traffic, citizen, enquired, inform, vehicles.

Plural Forms

Adding 's': car → cars, house → houses. Adding 'es': bus → buses, match → matches. Adding 'ies': story → stories, party → parties. We add -s to most singular nouns to make plural nouns. Some words require -es at the end to convert them to plural nouns. These words end in -s, -x, -ch and -sh. Some words that end in -o also require -es at the end to change them to plural nouns. Words that end in -y followed by a consonant are converted to plural nouns by replacing -y with -i and adding -es to the end.

Irregular Plurals

goose → geese, wolf → wolves, man → men, mouse → mice, ox → oxen, tooth → teeth. Irregular nouns do not follow any particular rule to change to plural nouns.

Plural Forms

child → children, book → books, calf → calves, foot → feet, city → cities.

Learning to Spell

The completed words are: citizen, inform, stranger, enquire, traffic.

Pointing Words

This is my favourite breakfast. That dress is beautiful. I like these vases. Those apples are very juicy. This, that, these and those are used with nouns to refer to people or things. We use 'this' and 'these' for people or things close to us. We use 'that' and 'those' for people or things away from us.

Pointing Words

This is my book. That is your bag. These are my shoes. Those are his books.

The Past Continuous Tense

Sahar and Sofia were playing. He was not writing a letter. We were getting late for the flight. They were running for a race. Was Salma going to Karachi? The past continuous tense is used to express an ongoing action in the past. Affirmative: Subject + was/were + base form of verb + -ing + object. Negative: Subject + was/were + not + base form of verb + -ing + object. Interrogative: Was/Were + subject + base form of verb + -ing + object?

The Past Continuous Tense

Affirmative: I was reading a book. They were playing cricket. Negative: I was not reading a book. They were not playing cricket. Interrogative: Was I reading a book? Were they playing cricket?

Connectors

Yesterday, I had a great time with my friends. Firstly, I met them in a park. Secondly, I bought a beautiful scarf for my sister and I went out to have dinner with my family. Finally, I returned home and completed my speech for the speech competition. Connectors are used to show the order in which things happen. 'Firstly', 'secondly' and 'then' are some connectors.

Connectors

Firstly, I wake up early in the morning. Secondly, I brush my teeth and take a bath. Then, I eat my breakfast and go to school. Finally, I return home and do my homework. This short paragraph uses connectors to show the sequence of a daily routine.

Hyphens

The hyphenated words are: well-known, thirty-two, mind-blowing, four-minute. He is a well-known writer. There are thirty-two students in my class. The show was mind-blowing. It was a four-minute walk to school. Hyphens are used to make compound numbers — The building has twenty-one floors; to join two words — Ahsan is a good-looking boy; and between the numbers in a fraction — He ate one-fourth of the bread.

Letter Writing

Dear Ali,

How are you? I am writing to share some traffic and safety rules for pedestrians. Always walk on the footpath. Cross only at zebra crossing. Look to your left and right before crossing the road. Never run on the road. Obey traffic signals and the traffic police.

Take care.

Your friend, Ahmed.

Letter conventions are: address, date, salutation, body, closing.

Expository Paragraph

My grandfather has given me a computer as a present. I am about to set up my new computer. There are so many different parts! I do not know where to start. The instructions manual can help me. It tells what each part is and how to attach it. I will follow the instructions step by step. First, I will connect the monitor and the (CPU). Next, I will connect the keyboard, mouse and speakers. Then, I will turn on the computer.

Expository Paragraph

First, I take a bag and check that it is clean. Next, I put my clothes in the bag. Then, I add my toothbrush, soap and towel. Finally, I put my books, water bottle and snacks in the bag, and I am ready for the trip. This is a short expository paragraph on how to pack a bag for a trip.

Creative Writing

Traffic rules can be followed in daily life in these ways: always walk on the footpath, cross at zebra crossing, look left and right, fasten the seatbelt in a car, and obey traffic signals.

lessons.notes_html:
Rainy Day

Umbrellas, raincoats and gumboots (long boots) are used to get shelter from rainwater. In the rain, a raincoat and gumboots can be worn and an umbrella can be taken. On a rainy day, hot pakoras and soup are good to eat. While it rains, indoor games like ludo can be played.

The Poem

Little drops of water,
Little grains of sand,
Make the mighty ocean
And the pleasant land.

So the little moments,
Humble though they may be,
Make the mighty ages
Of eternity.

So the little errors
Lead the soul away,
From the paths of virtue
Into sin to stray.

Little deeds of kindness,
Little words of love,
Make our earth an Eden,
Like the heaven above.

The poem 'Little Things' is by Julia A. Carney.

About the Poem

The poem is about how small things are important and make big things. Little things make a person happy because a kind word, a smile or a small gift can bring great joy.

The Meaning of Little

'Little' means small in size or amount. In this poem it also means humble and simple — but not useless, because little things together make mighty things.

The Last Stanza

The last stanza means that little deeds of kindness and little words of love make our earth like Eden (paradise), just like the heaven above. Small acts of kindness make the world a beautiful place.

An Act of Kindness

Once an old man was helped to cross the road and his bag was carried for him. He smiled and thanked the helper. He prayed for the helper. The helper felt very happy that day.

Rhyming Words

Pairs of rhyming words in the poem are: sand — land, away — stray, love — above. There is also the near-rhyme be — eternity.

An Act of Kindness

Once a lunch was shared with a classmate who had forgotten his lunch box. He was very happy and thanked the one who shared it.

Message of the Poem

The message is that little things are important and not useless. We should not look down upon them. Everything has its importance, no matter how little it may be. Little deeds of kindness and words of love make the world a heaven.

Map Directions

The direction of the post office from the school is West. The direction of the hospital from the playground is South-East. The direction of the playground from the hospital is North-West. The direction of the police station from the post office is South-East. On the map grid, the school is in the middle, the post office is to its west, the hospital is to its east, the playground is to the north, and the police station is to the south. The Direction Key is: North up, South down, West left, East right.

Key Facts

  • The poem 'Little Things' is written by Julia A. Carney.
  • The poem highlights the importance of little things.
  • Little grains of sand make the pleasant land.
  • An ocean is made up of little drops of water.

Analytical Reading

Activity: Use the internet and read about different rivers in Pakistan. Collect some interesting facts about them and share them with your classmates.

Stress, Rhythm and Intonation

Now another day is breaking. Sleep was sweet and so is waking. Dear Lord, I promised You last night never again to sulk or fight. Stress is the force used to pronounce words or syllables. Rhythm is the repeated pattern of sounds and movements. Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice while speaking. lessons.title: Language Focus and Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • eternity — infinite or unending time
  • pleasant — enjoyable
  • mighty — very large and powerful
  • stray — to lose direction
  • virtue — a good act

Regular Verb Forms

allow → allowed → allowed. behave → behaved → behaved. jump → jumped → jumped. talk → talked → talked. Past and past participles of regular verbs are formed by adding '-d' and '-ed'.

Regular Verb Forms

enjoy → enjoyed → enjoyed. kick → kicked → kicked. need → needed → needed. punish → punished → punished.

Learning to Spell

The correct spellings are: mighty, heaven, eternity, virtue, pleasant.

Question Words

The correct question words in order are: Where for the new school, Which for the storybook, What for the favourite game, Why for looking so happy, and Who for the person absent today. Question words are used to ask questions.

Question Words

When is used to ask about time or any occasion. Example: When will you go to Dubai? How many is used to ask about the number of countable nouns. Example: How many people work in his company? How much is used to ask about quantity and the price of uncountable nouns. Example: How much sugar would you like in your tea?

Question Words

Examples with When: When will you come to my house? When is your birthday? Examples with How many: How many books do you have? How many brothers do you have? Examples with How much: How much water do you drink daily? How much money do you have?

The Simple Future Tense

They will buy a new car at the end of this month. She will not go to school tomorrow. It will rain tomorrow. Will he plan starting a new business? I will play football with my friends. The student will not appear in the exams this year. The simple future tense refers to actions and events that will happen in future. Affirmative: Subject + will/shall + base form of verb + object. Negative: Subject + will/shall + not + base form of verb + object. Interrogative: Will/shall + subject + base form of verb + object?

The Simple Future Tense

I will visit my grandmother tomorrow. We will play cricket on Sunday. She will read a new book tonight. They will go to Murree in summer. He will buy a new bicycle next month.

Kinds of Sentences

Instructions: Fry the onion for 5-7 minutes. Take your medicine before sleeping. Read the given non-verbal cues. Commands: Clean your room. Sit down. Exclamatory Sentences: What a lovely waterfall! Wow, you won a gold medal! What a cold day! Command sentences are used to give commands. We use a full stop at the end of these sentences. These sentences are also called imperative sentences. Instructional sentences give instructions on how to do things. These sentences end in a full stop. Exclamatory sentences show sudden feelings and emotions. They end with an exclamation mark.

Kinds of Sentences

Do your chores after breakfast — Command. Serve drinks with the meal — Instruction. Wow, what a lovely dress! — Exclamatory.

Questions with Do and Does

Do you play hide and seek? — Yes, I play hide and seek. Do they live in Karachi? — No, they do not. Does she like Italian food? — Yes, she likes it very much. Does he work in a bank? — Yes, he does. Do and does are also used at the start of a sentence to ask a question. Such questions end with a question mark (?).

Questions with Do and Does

Do you like mangoes? Do they play hockey? Does she sing well? Does he go to school by bus?

Central Idea of the Poem

The poem 'Little Things' highlights the importance of little things. It teaches us that little things are not useless. Therefore, we should not look down upon them. Everything has its importance, no matter how little it may be.

Central Idea of the Third Stanza

The third stanza teaches us that little errors can lead the soul away from the paths of virtue into sin to stray — small mistakes, if repeated, can take a person away from goodness into wrongdoing.

Creative Writing: Rhyming Poem

Rhyming pairs: ball — tall, play — day, toys — joys, books — looks.

My favourite thing is my little ball,
I bounce it high against the wall.
I play with it all through the day,
And with my toys I laugh and play.

mcqs.q: What does 'eternity' mean?
mcqs.why: Eternity means infinite or unending time; pleasant means enjoyable and mighty means very large and powerful.

mcqs.q: What does 'virtue' mean?
mcqs.why: Virtue means a good act; stray means to lose direction, as little errors lead the soul away from the paths of virtue.

mcqs.q: What is the past form of 'allow'?
mcqs.why: Regular verbs form past and past participle by adding -d or -ed: allow → allowed → allowed, behave → behaved, jump → jumped.

mcqs.q: Which question word asks about time or an occasion?
mcqs.why: When is used to ask about time or any occasion: 'When will you go to Dubai?' How many asks about number and How much about quantity or price.

mcqs.q: 'How many' is used to ask about:
mcqs.why: How many asks about the number of countable nouns: 'How many books do you have?' How much asks about quantity and price of uncountable nouns.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is in the simple future tense?
options: She is going to school now.
She will not go to school tomorrow.
mcqs.why: The simple future tense refers to actions that will happen in future: Subject + will/shall + base form of verb, e.g. 'She will not go to school tomorrow.'

mcqs.q: Which sentence is a command?
options: Do you play hide and seek?
mcqs.why: Command sentences give commands and end with a full stop: 'Clean your room.' They are also called imperative sentences.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is exclamatory?
options: Wow, you won a gold medal!
mcqs.why: Exclamatory sentences show sudden feelings and emotions and end with an exclamation mark: 'Wow, you won a gold medal!'

mcqs.q: 'Do your chores after breakfast' is which kind of sentence?
mcqs.why: The lesson classifies 'Do your chores after breakfast' as a command, and 'Serve drinks with the meal' as an instruction.

mcqs.q: Which question uses 'Does' correctly?
mcqs.why: 'Does' is used with he/she/it: 'Does she like Italian food? — Yes, she likes it very much.' 'Do' is used with you/we/they.

lessons.title: Reading and Sounds Review
lessons.notes_html:
Intonation

Do you brush daily? — rising intonation, because it is a yes-no question. Where is your school? — falling intonation, because it is a wh-question. We should obey our parents. — falling intonation, because it is a statement. Hurrah! We have won the match. — falling intonation, because it is an exclamation.

Non-verbal Communication

The given signs say: celebration, angry, consoling. Non-verbal communication means using body parts and gestures to communicate feelings and emotions.

Talking to Strangers

If a stranger tries to be friendly, a student should not talk to him or accept anything from him. The student should step away, say 'No!', leave quickly and tell his or her parents or teacher. Nothing should ever be taken from a stranger, and everything should be shared with parents.

The Fox and the Stork

The fox invited the stork to his house to play a trick on him and make fun of him.

Traffic Rules

Three traffic rules are: Fasten your seatbelt. Cross only at zebra crossing. Always walk and never run. Other traffic rules are: follow traffic signals, obey traffic police, and look to your left and right before crossing the road.

Respect for Others

We should respect others because Allah (SWT) has made us all equal. Everyone has value, and we should never ridicule or degrade anyone for any reason.

Parts of Speech

  • Noun — fox, stork
  • Verb — invited, served
  • Pronoun — he, him
  • Adjective — clever, tasty
  • Adverb — happily, calmly
  • Preposition — in, to
  • Conjunction — and, but

options: To play a trick on him and make fun of him

Fasten your seatbelt; cross only at zebra crossing; always walk and never run

lessons.title: Language Focus and Writing Review
lessons.notes_html:
Vocabulary

  • harsh — severe, rough, unkind
  • degrade — to make people feel that they have no value
  • jogger — a person who runs slowly for exercise
  • stranger — a person that you do not know
  • mighty — very large and powerful

Tenses

The fox is degrading the stork — Present Continuous Tense. Did the children sleep late? — Simple Past Tense (interrogative). Ahsan takes out the brochure — Simple Present Tense. They will visit your house soon — Simple Future Tense. Ali was talking with his friend — Past Continuous Tense.

Hyphens

This building has thirty-four floors. He has eaten one-fourth of this cake. He is a well-known artist.

Kinds of Sentences

Instruction: Fry the onion for 5-7 minutes. Command: Clean your room. Exclamatory sentence: What a lovely waterfall!

Connectors

Sunday was a great day. I spent that day with my friends. Firstly, we visited the National Museum with our father. Secondly, we went to the nearby park and played cricket. Finally, we ate pizza and fries in the evening.

Story Writing: A Brave Girl

  • Character — a brave girl
  • Setting — her street
  • Plot — she sees a small boy in danger from a stray dog
  • Conflict — she is afraid but decides to act
  • Resolution — she saves the boy and everyone praises her bravery

Activity: Make a mind map about the topic 'A brave girl' and write a story with the help of the mind map.
